## Case intro session 1

You have been tasked with the responsibility as medical expert on a clinical trial. The projects' statistician want's you to give her some information in order for her to start her work.

-   Provide the mean and standard deviation of a prior study, so that she can compute power calculations.
-   Provide variables that you believe are medically relevant, based on medical expertise and prior studies.

The data is stored in `.csv` format and the company has provided you access to a GDPR-friendly and secure server where all the company data are stored. The only software installed on the server is `R` and `RStudio`.

:::{.hidden}

## Case intro session X

Søren, 45 yours old, Male, farther of three

Søren was recently diagnosed with cancer. The cancer is malignant but he's not particularly affected by it yet. The oncology team has proposed he could receive either chemotherapy, surgery, or radio therapy. He's unsure which treatment to opt in to. You read a paper in which the OR was x, y, z, the RR was x, y, z, and the AR was x, y, z.

Which recommendation would you give Søren?

## Case intro session Y

You notice a sub-group of the patients in the ICU die after leaving the ICU, while another sub-population recover well. You plan to test the mortality between the two in order to determine wither the sub-groups really differ.

Which considerations should you have?

## Case example 3

You work at a pharmaceutical company which is planning a clinical trial. The company wants to know how many patients to include. It turns out that your colleagues came up with different numbers between 100 and 1000. Which is correct and why did they come up with different answers?

The company want to go with the lowest level of patients due to economy. How can you evaluate this?

## Case example 5

You have been tasked to be the medical expert on a clinical trial. The projects' statistician want's you to draft a SAP for her. You need to give the statistician some information in order for her to start her work.

-   Define a clinically relevant effect.
-   Give him the mean and standard deviation of a prior study, so that he can make power calculations.
-   Provide variables that you believe are medically relevant, based on medical expertise and prior studies.

:::

## What do you make of this plot?

```{r first-plot}
#| echo: false
# output-location: slide

hd_data <- readr::read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanMazJen/medicinsk-statistik/main/data/hd_data.csv"
)

hd_data |>
  ggauto::ggauto(
    HD,
    MaxHR,
    title = "Coronary Heart Disease",
    subtitle = "303 individuals (139 Yes, 164 No) measured.",
    caption = "**Source**: Cleveland Medical Center",
    xlab = "Max Hear Rate",
    ylab = "Coronary Heart Disease"
  )
```


## What about this one?

```{r second-plot}
#| echo: false
# output-location: slide

hd_data <- readr::read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanMazJen/medicinsk-statistik/main/data/hd_data.csv"
)

hd_data |>

```

## Exploring the Heard Disease dataset

1)  Go to [**https://danmazjen.github.io/medicinsk-statistik**](https://danmazjen.github.io/medicinsk-statistik), exercises, and find the Cleveland Heart Disease dataset

2)  Copy the following code:

```r
hd_data <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanMazJen/medicinsk-statistik/main/data/hd_data.csv")
```

3)  Past it into your R console and check if you see the data in your `variable` pane.


## Code-along {auto-animate=true}

```r
library(ggplot2)                                # <1>

hd_data                                       # <2>
```

1. Tell R you will be using the `ggplot2` package
2. Take `hd_data`, and then,


## Code-along {auto-animate=true}

```r
library(ggplot2)                                # <1>

hd_data |>                                      # <2>
  ggplot(                                        # <3>
    aes(x = HD, y = Age)                    # <4>
    ) +                                          # <5>
  geom_boxplot()                                 # <6>
```

1. Tell R you will be using the `ggplot2` package
2. Take `hd_data`, and then,
3. Make a `ggplot` skeleton
4. Select the x and y variables using `aes` (aestetics)
5. End the ggplot function that has a parenthesis open. Add `+` more...
6. Specify the type of plot you want `ggplot` to do with the skeleton



# Medical Statistics

In this course, we will

-   develop statistical literacy skills
-   Learn to make medical inference from statistics
-   Perform statistics using R

## Develop statistical literacy skills

::: {.fragment}
What does it mean to have an odds ratio of 0.9?
:::

::: {.fragment}
Is it good or bad for my patient that a study concluded `OR: 0.9` for a 5 year mortality risk?
:::

::: {.fragment}
When informing my patient about surgery, should I use the relative risk or absolute risk difference?
:::
